Missing `--from/--to`: exit 2, prints error and help (via cli.ts logic). - `--dry-run`: exit 0, file content unchanged, logs dry-run summary. - Safety/UX: - No subcommand: prints help, exits 0, no error logs. - tests/perf/maintenance-large-workspace.test.ts: - Creates a large synthetic workspace (10 modules × 50 files, 250 story files, a mix of valid and stale references). - Asserts that: - `detectStaleAnnotations` finds stale entries and runs in < 5000 ms. - tests/perf/maintenance-cli-large-workspace.test.ts: - Similar large-workspace tests at CLI level for `detect --json`, `report --format=json`, and `verify --root ...`, all under 5 seconds and with correct payloads/messages. - These tests demonstrate that maintenance operations are performant and suitable for large codebases, supporting the Quality Standards acceptance criterion.,Safety and non-destructiveness (REQ-MAINT-SAFE across layers): - getAllFiles in src/maintenance/utils.ts validates that the path exists and is a directory before traversal, returning [] otherwise. - CLI-level safety: - `runMaintenanceCli` wraps command dispatch in a try/catch, logs a clear `traceability-maint failed: ` error, and returns EXIT_USAGE on unhandled errors, as confirmed by the permission error test. - traceability.notes: The story docs/stories/009.0-DEV-MAINTENANCE-TOOLS.story.md describes a set of maintenance tools for detecting stale @story annotations, updating references, batching changes, verifying post-conditions, generating reports, and ensuring operations are safe and user-friendly. All enumerated requirements (REQ-MAINT-DETECT, REQ-MAINT-UPDATE, REQ-MAINT-BATCH, REQ-MAINT-VERIFY, REQ-MAINT-REPORT, REQ-MAINT-SAFE) are implemented in src/maintenance/* and wired into both a programmatic API and the `traceability-maint` CLI. There is extensive, story-traced test coverage (unit, integration, and performance) validating behavior, edge cases, safety, and performance on large workspaces. User-facing documentation for the Maintenance CLI and its usage is present in README.md and referenced user docs. Based on the concrete code and passing tests tied directly to this story, all acceptance criteria are satisfied.
